name: Narrative Transportation
description: Becoming absorbed into a story -- engaged imagery, affect, and attentional focus -- produces stronger shifts toward the story's own beliefs, more favorable views of its protagonists, and reduced scrutiny of factual inconsistencies within it.
design_relevance_note: The mechanism behind case-study-driven marketing copy, founder-story brand pages, and testimonial-led onboarding -- a story that genuinely absorbs the reader persuades more, and does so partly by lowering critical scrutiny, which is worth naming honestly rather than treating storytelling as a neutral technique.
prevalence_note: The named concept behind 'storytelling sells' as a design/marketing maxim, though the specific term 'transportation' is more academic than the practice built on it.

findings.description: Readers who report greater 'transportation' (narrative absorption involving imagery, affect, and attentional focus) into a story show stronger shifts toward story-consistent beliefs and more favorable evaluations of the story's protagonists, and notice fewer factual inconsistencies in the narrative; experimentally reducing transportation via processing instructions reduces these belief and evaluation shifts.
findings.source_title: The Role of Transportation in the Persuasiveness of Public Narratives
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

applications.title: Dove's 'Real Beauty Sketches': a personal narrative structure that reached 163 million views by mid-2013
applications.description: Unilever's Dove brand, working with ad agency Ogilvy & Mather (Brazil), released 'Real Beauty Sketches' on April 14, 2013: a forensic sketch artist, working behind a curtain, drew each of several women twice -- once from her own self-description, once from a stranger's description of the same woman -- then revealed the two sketches side by side, with the stranger-based version consistently more flattering and more accurate than the woman's own. The video's structure is a deliberate narrative arc (anticipation, reveal, emotional payoff for each subject) built specifically to draw viewers into the story rather than simply state a claim about self-perception. The real, disclosed reach: 30.6 million views for the 3-minute cut within two weeks (97.6% positive feedback), 660,000 Facebook shares in the first ten days, and 163 million global views with 4.6 billion total media impressions by June 2013.
applications.ethical_note: The campaign's message (people are more beautiful than they believe) was widely experienced as genuinely affirming, and no one is misled about facts. But it was also, real and lastingly, criticized by commentators as a beauty-and-personal-care brand commercially benefiting from first naming and dwelling on women's self-image insecurity before offering reassurance -- a real, unresolved tension between authentic emotional value and its use as a commercial vehicle, not a clean case either way.
